stem: Organisms too small to be seen with the naked eye are called __________.
solution: Microorganisms are tiny living things visible only under a microscope.

stem: Microorganisms are studied with the help of a __________.
solution: A microscope magnifies microbes enough to be seen and studied.

stem: The four major groups of microorganisms are bacteria, fungi, protozoa and __________.
solution: Microorganisms are grouped as bacteria, fungi, protozoa and algae; viruses are a special group that reproduce only inside a host.

stem: Which of the following is a bacterial disease in humans?
solution: Tuberculosis and typhoid are bacterial diseases; common cold and polio are viral; malaria is caused by a protozoan.

stem: Which of the following is a viral disease?
solution: Common cold, influenza and polio are viral; typhoid, cholera and TB are bacterial.

stem: Malaria is caused by a protozoan called __________, spread by the female Anopheles mosquito.
solution: The malarial parasite Plasmodium is spread by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito.

stem: Diseases that spread from an infected person to a healthy person are called __________.
solution: Communicable diseases spread from an infected person to others through air, water, food or carriers.

stem: Animals or insects that carry disease-causing microbes from one person to another are called __________.
solution: Carriers (vectors) like mosquitoes and houseflies transmit disease-causing microbes.

stem: The housefly can spread diseases like cholera and typhoid because it __________.
options: carries microbes from filth to food
solution: Houseflies pick up microbes from waste and deposit them on food, spreading diseases like cholera and typhoid.

stem: A medicine that kills or stops the growth of disease-causing microorganisms is called an __________.
solution: Antibiotics kill or stop the growth of harmful microbes; e.g., penicillin.

stem: The first antibiotic, penicillin, was discovered by __________.
solution: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin, the first antibiotic, from a mould.

stem: Antibiotics should be taken __________.
options: only on a doctor's advice and for the full course
solution: Antibiotics must be taken only as prescribed and for the full course; misuse makes microbes resistant.

stem: A preparation that provides immunity against a disease by introducing dead or weakened microbes is called a __________.
solution: A vaccine contains dead or weakened microbes that trigger the body to build immunity against a disease.

stem: The vaccine against smallpox was developed by __________.
solution: Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine, against smallpox.

stem: The process of adding dead/weakened microbes to protect the body against a disease is called __________.
solution: Vaccination introduces a vaccine into the body to develop immunity against a disease.

stem: Curd is formed from milk by the action of the bacterium __________.
solution: Lactobacillus converts milk into curd through fermentation.

stem: Yeast is used in the baking of bread because it produces __________ during fermentation, making the dough rise.
solution: Yeast ferments sugar to produce carbon dioxide, which makes the dough rise.

stem: The process by which microorganisms convert sugar into alcohol is called __________.
solution: Fermentation by yeast converts sugars into alcohol and carbon dioxide; discovered by Louis Pasteur.

stem: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria such as Rhizobium live in the root nodules of __________.
solution: Rhizobium in the root nodules of legumes fixes atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form.

stem: Microorganisms help make the soil fertile by fixing nitrogen and by __________.
options: decomposing dead plants and animals into humus
solution: Microbes decompose dead matter into nutrient-rich humus and fix nitrogen, enriching the soil.

stem: The atmospheric nitrogen (about 78% of air) is converted into usable compounds by __________.
solution: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria (and lightning) convert atmospheric nitrogen into compounds usable by plants — part of the nitrogen cycle.

stem: Which of the following is a disease-causing microorganism (a 'foe')?
solution: The TB-causing bacterium is harmful (a foe); the others are useful (friendly) microorganisms.

stem: Food that has been spoiled by microorganisms should not be eaten because it may cause __________.
solution: Microbes and their toxins in spoiled food can cause food poisoning.

stem: Adding salt or edible oil to pickles helps preserve food because these __________.
options: prevent the growth of spoilage microbes
solution: Salt and oil create conditions unfavourable for microbes, preserving pickles and other foods.

stem: The method of preserving milk by heating and then rapidly cooling it is called __________.
solution: Pasteurisation heats milk to kill microbes and then cools it quickly, extending its shelf life.

stem: Which of the following is a common method of food preservation?
options: Salting, sugaring, drying, boiling and refrigeration
solution: Salting, sugaring, drying, boiling and refrigeration all slow or prevent microbial spoilage of food.

stem: Common chemical preservatives added to jams and squashes include __________.
solution: Chemical preservatives like sodium benzoate and sodium metabisulphite prevent spoilage of jams and squashes.

stem: Which of the following diseases affects plants and is caused by microorganisms?
solution: Citrus canker is a bacterial plant disease; the others affect humans.

stem: Which of the following microorganisms can be seen only with an electron microscope and reproduces only inside a host?
solution: Viruses are extremely small and reproduce only inside a host cell.

stem: Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) fix nitrogen and are useful in __________ fields.
solution: Blue-green algae fix nitrogen in paddy fields, acting as a natural biofertiliser.

stem: The malaria-carrying mosquito is the female __________ mosquito.
solution: The female Anopheles mosquito carries the malarial parasite Plasmodium.

stem: The disease dengue is spread by the __________ mosquito.
solution: Dengue is spread by the Aedes mosquito.

stem: To prevent mosquito-borne diseases, we should __________.
options: not allow water to collect and breed mosquitoes
solution: Preventing water from stagnating removes mosquito breeding grounds, reducing diseases like malaria and dengue.

stem: Microorganisms are useful in medicine to produce __________.
solution: Microbes are used to make antibiotics and vaccines, which fight and prevent diseases.

stem: Which microorganism is used to make alcohol and wine?
solution: Yeast ferments sugars to make alcohol used in wine and other beverages.

stem: The commercial production of alcohol and wine from grains and fruit juices is done through __________.
solution: Yeast ferments the sugars in grains and fruit juices to produce alcohol commercially.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a microorganism with its use?
solution: Lactobacillus makes curd. (Yeast bakes bread, Rhizobium fixes nitrogen, Plasmodium causes malaria.)

stem: Which of the following is NOT a communicable disease?
solution: Scurvy is a deficiency disease (vitamin C), not communicable; the others spread from person to person.

stem: Antibiotics are NOT effective against __________.
solution: Antibiotics work against bacteria and some other microbes but not against viruses.

stem: The nitrogen cycle keeps the amount of nitrogen in the atmosphere __________.
solution: The nitrogen cycle balances nitrogen fixation and return, keeping atmospheric nitrogen roughly constant.

stem: Some fungi like Rhizopus (bread mould) can be harmful because they __________.
solution: Moulds like Rhizopus spoil bread and other foods, making them a foe.

stem: Which of the following is a friendly role of microorganisms in the environment?
options: Decomposing dead matter and cleaning the environment
solution: Decomposer microbes break down dead matter and waste, cleaning up the environment and recycling nutrients.

stem: Refrigeration preserves food by __________.
options: slowing down the growth of microbes at low temperature
solution: Low temperatures in a refrigerator slow microbial growth, keeping food fresh longer.

stem: Which of the following is caused by a protozoan?
solution: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium; typhoid and TB are bacterial and cold is viral.

stem: Boiling drinking water is a good habit because it __________.
solution: Boiling kills harmful microbes in water, making it safe to drink.

stem: The disease anthrax, affecting animals and humans, is caused by a __________.
solution: Anthrax is a bacterial disease affecting cattle and humans.

stem: Which of the following food items uses microbial fermentation?
solution: Idli/dosa batter and cheese are made using microbial fermentation.

stem: Which practice reduces the spread of communicable diseases?
options: Maintaining cleanliness, drinking safe water and getting vaccinated
solution: Cleanliness, safe water, and vaccination reduce the spread of communicable diseases.

stem: Which of the following is used as a biofertiliser to enrich soil with nitrogen?
solution: Blue-green algae and Rhizobium fix nitrogen and act as natural biofertilisers.

stem: Which of the following is a fungal microorganism?
solution: Bread mould (Rhizopus) is a fungus; Amoeba is a protozoan, Lactobacillus a bacterium.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Microorganisms: Friend and Foe' is that:
options: microorganisms can be both harmful (causing diseases and spoiling food) and helpful (in curd-making, medicine, soil fertility and decomposition)
microbes have no effect on us
solution: The chapter shows that microbes have both harmful roles (diseases, food spoilage) and beneficial roles (fermentation, medicine, nitrogen fixation, decomposition).

stem: Viruses reproduce only inside the cells of a __________.
solution: Viruses can reproduce only inside a living host cell.

stem: Curd is formed from milk by the action of __________.
solution: Lactobacillus bacteria convert milk into curd.

stem: The microorganism used to make bread and in brewing is __________.
solution: Yeast, a fungus, is used in baking and brewing through fermentation.

stem: The process by which yeast produces alcohol from sugar is called __________.
solution: Fermentation is the breakdown of sugar by yeast, producing alcohol and carbon dioxide.

stem: The scientist who discovered the process of fermentation was __________.
solution: Louis Pasteur discovered fermentation.

stem: A substance that provides immunity against a specific disease is a __________.
solution: A vaccine gives immunity by preparing the body to fight a disease.

stem: Medicines that kill or stop the growth of disease-causing microbes are __________.
solution: Antibiotics kill or inhibit disease-causing microbes, especially bacteria.

stem: Malaria is caused by a protozoan carried by the female __________ mosquito.
solution: The malarial parasite is spread by the female Anopheles mosquito.

stem: Dengue is spread by the __________ mosquito.
solution: Dengue is spread by the Aedes mosquito.

stem: An organism that spreads disease from one host to another is called a __________.
solution: A vector, such as a mosquito, carries pathogens between hosts.

stem: A disease that spreads from an infected person to a healthy one is called __________.
solution: Communicable diseases spread from person to person.

stem: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria live in the root nodules of __________ plants.
solution: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria live in the root nodules of leguminous plants.

stem: Microorganisms that decompose dead plants and animals are called __________.
solution: Decomposers break down dead matter, recycling nutrients.

stem: Heating milk and cooling it quickly to kill harmful microbes is called __________.
solution: Pasteurisation heats and rapidly cools milk to destroy harmful microbes.

stem: Adding salt or sugar preserves food by __________.
options: removing water and checking microbial growth
solution: Salt and sugar draw out water by osmosis, preventing microbial growth.

stem: The chemicals added to food to prevent spoilage are called __________.
solution: Preservatives prevent microbial spoilage of food.

stem: The smallpox vaccine was developed by __________.
solution: Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine, against smallpox.

stem: Which of these diseases is caused by a virus?
solution: The common cold is viral; the others are bacterial.

stem: Which of these diseases is caused by bacteria?
solution: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease; the others are viral.

stem: Cholera and typhoid spread mainly through __________.
solution: Cholera and typhoid are water- and food-borne diseases.

stem: The nitrogen cycle is maintained with the help of __________.
solution: Microorganisms fix and recycle nitrogen, maintaining the nitrogen cycle.

stem: Blue-green algae in fields are useful because they __________.
solution: Some blue-green algae fix nitrogen, naturally enriching the soil.

stem: Food poisoning results from eating food in which harmful __________ have grown.
solution: Harmful microbes multiplying in food produce toxins that cause food poisoning.

stem: Boiling drinking water makes it safer because it __________.
solution: Boiling kills most disease-causing microorganisms.

stem: Which of the following is a beneficial use of microorganisms?
solution: Microorganisms are used beneficially to make antibiotics, curd, bread and more.

stem: Rhizobium bacteria benefit plants by __________.
solution: Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes.

stem: The medicine that gives long-lasting protection against a disease works by building __________.
solution: Vaccines build immunity, giving long-lasting protection against a disease.

stem: Which of these is a fungal disease?
solution: Ringworm is caused by a fungus.
